### Motivation

- The governance evaluation marked authoritative source documents as irrelevant due to legacy `source_document` values not being parsed or normalized into `relevant_document_ids`, causing retrieval metrics to be computed against mismatched IDs. 
- Retrieved chunk/document identifiers produced by the dispatcher and retriever used inconsistent shapes and path formats (Windows separators, `/app/data/raw/` prefixes, duplicate slashes, case differences) that prevented correct matching. 
- The scoring logic treated repeated chunks and document-level judgments inconsistently, resulting in incorrect Precision/Recall/MRR/NDCG values for cases with duplicate chunks from the same document.

### Description

- Map legacy `source_document` workbook field into `relevant_document_ids` while preserving the original `source_document` value in `source_fields` and supporting scalar, JSON, comma/semicolon/pipe/newline-delimited lists and N/A handling via improved `_list` parsing in `benchmark_loader.py`.

- Normalize dispatcher outputs (`ExecutionDispatcher._normalize_chunks`) and update scoring (`retrieval_scores`) to: prefer chunk-level judgments when present, compare normalized document IDs otherwise, count duplicate relevant chunks at their returned ranks for Precision@5, MRR, and NDCG@5, and deduplicate when computing Recall@5 so each relevant document contributes at most once.

items.title: oss pick: what to work on next, scored against what you have already done
items.body:
Every backlog tool ranks by the same public signals — reactions, labels, age, comment count. Those say what is **popular**. None say what is **yours**: which of four hundred open issues sits in the part of the codebase you have already read, argued about and fixed.

This scores the backlog against your own corpus. **Reviews count 4× a note**, because reviewing something is the one place you demonstrably read the code rather than saved a link.

### It works, and you can check it
```
2.23  #3816  InstantPatternLegacyFormatter computes precision incorrectly
      because you wrote: #4220 — the instant pattern precision review
1.51  #3369  LoggerConfig.RootLogger.Builder#withtFilter (typo)
      because you wrote: #4224 — the withFilter alias review
```
Neither shares a label or milestone with what it matched. They share the thing that matters — and only a corpus of your own work knows it.

**No model needed.** Term overlap against your own writing is arithmetic and runs on a machine with nothing installed.

Built entirely on what core already had: `ReviewLedger`, `BuiltinMemory`, `TextIndex`. The Python original scored against a DEVONthink archive, so it only worked for someone who had one.

An attached memory extension is **deliberately not consulted yet** — every archive stores things differently, and guessing at someone's layout would produce confident nonsense.

Also moves the backlog cache out of the current working directory: relative `.triage-cache/` was fine for a checkout script, but as an installed command it litters every directory it runs from and two runs from two places silently don't share a cache.

items.title: [codex] Fix native solver correctness and prepare huge 2.0.0
items.body:
## Summary

This prepares a 2.0.0 correctness and release-hardening update for both the R
`huge` package and the native Python `pyhuge` package. It fixes the TIGER
covariance/raw-data boundary, moves TIGER correlation construction and
automatic lambda selection into the shared C++ core, strengthens solver and
input contracts, reduces path memory, and validates the installed CMake and
PyPI artifacts.

## Problem and user impact

TIGER input semantics were split across the R/Python frontends and the native
solver. A symmetric square matrix could be classified as covariance input but
then be consumed as raw observations, while the lambda path could be selected
from a different matrix than the one actually solved. This made raw-data,
covariance, R, and Python paths inconsistent and could return incorrect
precision estimates.

Several native paths also lacked a common finite/shape/path contract, complete
KKT certification, and convergence-status propagation. At difficult scales or
small lambda values this could expose asymmetric, unstable, or incompletely
converged results. Python MB/TIGER adapters additionally expanded sparse
support into dense `nlambda * d * d` storage, and RIC/StARS could allocate more
workers and scratch memory than the requested tasks required.

## Root cause and fix

- Add explicit `auto`, `data`, and `covariance` input routing in R and Python.
  TIGER now passes the original matrix plus the resolved input flag to the
  shared C++ core.
- Construct and validate the covariance/correlation matrix once in C++, select
  automatic TIGER lambda values from that same matrix, and solve the
  correlation-domain square-root Lasso with full KKT certification.
- Stabilize covariance normalization and lambda generation at extreme scales;
  validate symmetry, PSD, finite values, dimensions, and method-specific path
  ordering at both public and native boundaries.
- Return only the longest certified automatic TIGER prefix and fail closed for
  uncertifiable explicit values. Propagate iteration-budget warnings instead
  of silently returning partial convergence.
- Fix precision/graph symmetry, one-variable handling, RIC scale dependence,
  generator and NPN parity, ROC/inference validation, and graphics-state
  restoration.
- Consume compressed native MB/TIGER support directly, stream StARS
  accumulation, and cap RIC/StARS workers to available tasks.
- Repair standalone CMake BLAS/OpenMP exports and installed consumers. Harden
  PyPI source/wheel checks, native ABI coverage, license packaging, and R/Python
  parity gates.
- Set R `huge`, Python `pyhuge`, CMake metadata, NEWS, changelog, and release
  documentation to version 2.0.0.

The default automatic routing remains compatible. Callers with square,
symmetric raw observations can now select `data` explicitly. TIGER+StARS
currently fails fast until subsample fits expose a common certified path
prefix; Python native source builds explicitly support Linux and macOS.

## Validation

- Full Python pytest suite passed against the isolated R `huge 2.0.0` build,
  including R/Python parity.
- `R CMD check --no-manual`: 0 errors, 1 warning, 0 notes. The warning is from
  the local R header/Apple Clang warning-group combination, not package code.
- Static and shared installed CMake consumer smoke tests passed.
- Nineteen packaging, CMake, and R-build contract tests passed.
- Three R/Python shared-core mirror pairs are byte-identical.
- `mkdocs build --strict` passed.
- The `pyhuge-2.0.0` sdist passed `twine check`; an out-of-checkout install
  reported version 2.0.0 and passed native MB/TIGER smoke tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.

items.title: Normalize query/doc ID matching in evaluation to fix zero/incorrect precision and recall
items.body:
The retrieval pipeline was returning valid hits, but evaluation often computed zero/incorrect precision and recall due to mismatched identifiers between retrieved results and ground-truth entries. The fix aligns query and document identity handling across evaluation paths so relevance comparisons are performed on canonical values.

- **Root cause addressed: canonicalization gap in evaluation**
  - Added a shared `EvaluationNormalizer` to normalize:
    - query strings (trim, quote removal, whitespace collapse, lowercase)
    - document IDs (path separator normalization, `./` cleanup, canonical tail form, lowercase)
  - This removes false negatives caused by equivalent-but-different string forms.

- **Ground-truth consistency**
  - Updated `GroundTruth` to store normalized query keys and normalized relevant document IDs.
  - Updated lookup (`getRelevantDocs`) to normalize incoming query text before map access.

- **Precision/recall computation alignment**
  - Updated `EvaluationService` and `Evaluator` to compare normalized retrieved IDs vs normalized relevant IDs.
  - Centralized relevant-hit counting in shared normalization-aware logic, including controlled filename fallback when one side is unqualified.

- **Net effect**
  - Precision and recall now reflect actual overlap between retrieved results and judgments instead of string-format artifacts.

```java
// before: direct string comparison could miss equivalent IDs
relevantDocs.contains(result.getDocumentId());

// now: both sides compared in normalized canonical form
String docId = EvaluationNormalizer.normalizeDocId(result.getDocumentId());
long relevantRetrieved = EvaluationNormalizer.countRelevantRetrieved(
    retrievedNormalizedDocs,
    relevantNormalizedDocs
);
```

milestone.description: Warnings for deprecated text outputs, fixes, possibly new features

items.body:
A couple simple string typos were fixed, plus two other issues.

`tt` and `tb` are pointer parameters (`double *tt`, `double *tb`), so `tt - tb` computes pointer difference (an address offset), not the difference between the pointed-to text box values. The condition should dereference the pointers: `(*tt - *tb) > YTIC_DIST`.

The format string `"%f.0"` is incorrect — the `.0` precision specifier must be inside the format specifier, not after it. The literal `.0` will be appended as plain text to the output. The intended format is `"%.0f"` to format the value as a float with no decimal places.

items.body:
## Summary

PR #5 built the Fargate/EventBridge Scheduler infra and passed CI, but CI only exercises `dev`/DuckDB. Actually deploying to AWS and running the task against real Athena/Iceberg surfaced several real bugs, all fixed and verified with live end-to-end runs:

- **Dockerfile**: install `gcc` (`build-essential`) — `mmh3` (transitive dep of `dbt-athena-community`) has no prebuilt wheel for this platform/Python combo and fails to compile without it.
- **infra**: the `jaffle_shop`/`raw` Glue Databases already existed in this AWS account from prior dbt Cloud runs (with real data — 47 tables). The stack was wrongly trying to *create* them (`CREATE_FAILED: AlreadyExists`), which also meant a future `cdk destroy` would have deleted real data. Now the stack only references them by name via IAM; never creates or destroys them.
- **infra**: task role was missing `glue:GetTableVersion(s)`, blocking every staging view that reads via `source()`.
- **dbt**: dbt-athena's macro dispatch has no `athena__convert_timezone`, so it fell back to a Postgres-only `::numeric` cast Trino rejects (`metricflow_time_spine` failed with `FUNCTION_NOT_FOUND`). Added a local `athena__convert_timezone` shim delegating to dbt_date's existing `trino__` implementation.
- **dbt**: scoped one `stg_locations` unit test out of the `prod` target — a dbt-athena/Iceberg unit-test-framework timestamp precision limitation (`NOT_SUPPORTED: Incorrect timestamp precision for timestamp(6)`) unrelated to the model itself, which builds fine on prod.

Plus two cleanups found along the way:
- **Dockerfile**: build with `uv sync --frozen` instead of `uv venv && pip install -r requirements.txt`, so `uv run` doesn't silently re-sync (downloading `ty`/`ruff`/`botocore`) on every single invocation.
- **dbt**: nested 8 generic test configs under `arguments:` to clear `MissingArgumentsPropertyInGenericTestDeprecation` warnings.
- **infra**: build/run on Graviton (ARM64) instead of the Fargate X86_64 default — cheaper, and matches arm64 dev machines for native local `docker build` (no more QEMU emulation).

items.title: Fix model viewer shell bleed-through and facet shading
items.body:
## What changed

- request a 24-bit depth buffer and use opaque `GL_LESS` depth testing
- tighten model-view near/far clip planes so the build plate no longer destroys depth precision around small models
- rebuild STL facet normals from triangle vertices instead of trusting stale exported normals
- add regression tests for clip-plane precision and incorrect ASCII/binary STL normals

## Why

The model in the reported screenshot was fully opaque in the fragment shader, but the viewer combined a near plane of `0.05` mm with a far plane hundreds of millimetres away. On a mobile depth buffer this can let hidden/coplanar triangles win depth tests and look like transparency. The imported STL normals could also be valid numbers but point in unrelated directions, producing the large triangular light/dark patches.

The fix addresses both causes without enabling back-face culling, so open or imperfect printable STLs remain visible rather than losing faces.

### Related Issues/PRs Closes #23991 ### What changes are proposed in this pull request? `mlflow.evaluate(model_type="classifier")` computed the binary `precision_recall_auc` and the ROC / precision-recall / calibration **curve artifacts** against a hardcoded probability column (`y_probs[:, 1]`). `_validate_label_list` reorders `label_list` so `pos_label` is last, but the predicted-probability columns stay in the model's (sorted) class order. As a result, when `pos_label` is **not** the higher-sorted class: - `precision_recall_auc` is wrong (e.g. `0.32` instead of `~0.99` on a separable problem), - the ROC / precision-recall / calibration curve plots are produced for the wrong class. items.title: fix(b20-stablecoin): hard-code decimals to 6 to eliminate zero-return window
items.body:
[BOP-342](https://linear.app/coinbase/issue/BOP-342) [BOP-349](https://linear.app/coinbase/issue/BOP-349)

## Motivation

`B20StablecoinToken::decimals()` previously delegated to the storage adapter via `TokenAccounting::decimals()`, which returns `0` for an uninitialized slot. During the factory bootstrap window -- after `set_code` installs the marker bytecode but before the `initCalls` chain writes the token fields -- any external call to `decimals()` would return `0` instead of the correct stablecoin precision of `6`. This is incorrect: stablecoin precision is a protocol-level constant, not a per-token configuration value.

## What changed

- In `B20StablecoinToken`'s dispatch, the `decimals` selector now returns `B20Variant::Stablecoin.decimals()` (always `6`) instead of reading from the `TokenAccounting` storage adapter.
- A unit test is added verifying that `decimals()` returns `6` regardless of the value held in the backing accounting (including `0`, which simulates the uninitialized-slot case).

## What was tried / considered

The recommendation in the audit finding suggested adding a method override directly on `B20StablecoinToken`. Because the dispatch layer already handles per-variant logic and `B20Variant::Stablecoin.decimals()` already encodes this constant (used by the factory storage when emitting `B20Created`), routing through that existing constant keeps the source of truth in one place and avoids adding a new method to the trait hierarchy.

items.title: Hero Demo #1: cross-source company resolution (SEC EDGAR + GLEIF)
items.body:
## Summary

Adds Linkuity's first **showcase** (`showcases/company-resolution/`) — a polished, self-contained demo that resolves **49 real US companies** across two independent public systems, **SEC EDGAR** and **GLEIF**, that share *no* common identifier. Resolution runs on company **name + address only**; the CIK↔LEI crosswalk is held out and used purely to validate.

Also introduces the top-level `showcases/` directory (distinct from `samples/`: samples are small teaching datasets for learning matching config; showcases are end-to-end demos on real public data) and a `showcases/README.md` catalog.

## Result (machine-verified, reproducible)

- 107 source records → **60 golden records**
- **38 / 49 companies correctly unified**, **0 incorrect merges**
- **Precision 100.0% · Recall 80.6% · F1 89.2%**

Zero false merges is the hard gate — enforced by both a PowerShell scorecard (`validate/Test-Resolution.ps1`) and a C# regression test (`CompanyResolutionDemoTests`), which pins the golden count and asserts no cluster mixes two companies.

## Why it's convincing (and honest)

- **No cheat key.** SEC keys on CIK, GLEIF on LEI — they don't overlap, so resolution must work from a fuzzy name and a postal address. Identifiers never enter `run/companies.csv` or the profile; they live only in `validate/ground-truth.csv`.
- **Real data, projected verbatim.** Every name/address comes byte-for-byte from the live APIs (e.g. a malformed `98027-` ZIP and lowercase `c/o` survive untouched). The only "duplicates" are genuine SEC `formerNames` records.
- **Failures shown, not hidden.** The 11 split companies are reported with reasons — e.g. GLEIF `THE BOEING COMPANY` vs SEC `BOEING CO` never become match candidates, and true rebrands (Bell Atlantic→Verizon) can't bridge on name alone.

## Notable decisions

- **Dropped Chevron:** its NYSE parent has no LEI in GLEIF at all, so pairing it would mix a parent SEC record with a subsidiary GLEIF record. 49 honest pairs over 50 with an asterisk.
- **GLEIF headquarters address, not legal address:** GLEIF's *legal* address is frequently a shared Delaware registered-agent address (noise that even caused a Boeing+Disney false merge and capped unification at 24/49). Projecting the real *headquarters* address lifted it to 38/49 and eliminated the false-merge ceiling. This is disclosed transparently in the showcase README.

## What's included

`showcases/company-resolution/`:
- `acquire/Get-Sources.ps1` + `prepare/Build-Input.ps1` — live SEC+GLEIF fetch → committed input (offline-runnable; `-Refresh` re-pulls)
- `run/` — committed `companies.csv`, tuned `company.profile.json` + `company.merge.json`, pinned `expectations.json`
- `validate/` — scorecard + held-out `ground-truth.csv`
- `run-demo.ps1` — one command: run → validate (`-Neo4j` also emits a graph export)
- `assets/` — mermaid pipeline diagram, golden-org graph, VHS recording tape
- Flagship `README.md` with verified numbers and side-by-side match examples

Repo wiring: `showcases/README.md` catalog, a single link line from the root README, `.gitignore` for generated output/cache.

## Scope / safety

- **Config-only** — the sole C# added is the one regression test (`CompanyResolutionDemoTests`). No engine/production code changed.
- Full suite green (**498 tests**). Clean-clone `./run-demo.ps1` runs offline and reproduces 60/0/100%.
- Data licensing: GLEIF is CC0; SEC EDGAR is US-government public domain (attributed in the README).

items.title: Org blocking 2a: name canonicalizer + fingerprint strategy (measured, 25x workload cut)
items.body:
## Summary

First installment of the blocking-improvement track (spec 2a of 2a/2b/2c): an **organization-name canonicalizer** and a **fingerprint blocking strategy**, replacing the brittle `token-name` last-token keying in organization profiles. Measured end-to-end with the blocking audit instrument (#26) against the company-resolution showcase.

Org profiles (built-in + showcase) now block on `["exact-value", "fingerprint", "phonetic", "prefix"]`.

## What's included

- **`OrganizationNameCanonicalizer`** (`Linkuity.Matching.Canonicalization`, blocking-only — `FieldNormalizer`/scoring/stored data untouched): uppercase, punctuation folding (periods/apostrophes deleted), ampersand-initial collapse (`AT & T` → `ATT`), leading-article drop with single-letter guard (`THE BOEING COMPANY` → `BOEING`, but `A O SMITH` keeps its `A`), repeated trailing legal-suffix stripping against a curated international list (~40 entries incl. `GMBH`, `SA`, `PLC`, `SAB DE CV`; `GROUP` deliberately excluded). Never strips below one token.
- **`FingerprintBlockingStrategy`** (`fp:{sorted deduped canonical tokens}`): word-order, article, punctuation, and suffix variants land in one block (`THE WALT DISNEY COMPANY` ≡ `WALT DISNEY CO` → `fp:disney walt`). Semantic-type-driven via a pluggable `ITokenCanonicalizer` map — person/address/product fingerprinting can register later without touching the strategy.
- **Phonetic alignment**: `PhoneticBlockingStrategy`'s org branch now keys the first *canonical* token (one shared definition of "the distinctive token"); person branches unchanged.
- **Showcase re-baselined** with the measured numbers, `--min-recall 0.87` CI gate wired into `run-demo.ps1 -AuditBlocking`, `mustUnify` extended with the newly-unifying companies.

## Measured results (company-resolution showcase, via `match blocking audit`)

| Metric | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Recall ceiling | 87.5% (4 fixable misses + 5 renames) | 87.5% (**all 9 misses are renames**) |
| Boeing / Disney / Coca-Cola / P&G pairs | unreachable | **reachable** |
| Candidate pairs (workload) | 1,761 | **71** |
| Largest block | `name:inc` (56 records) | 5 |
| Incorrect merges / precision | 0 / 100% | 0 / 100% |
| Correctly unified | 38 | **39** (Coca-Cola & P&G now unify) |
| Pairwise recall | 80.6% | 77.8% |

**On the recall dip (honest trade, documented in the README):** the old `name:inc` mega-block accidentally made rename pairs (`AT&T` ↔ `SBC`, `META` ↔ `FACEBOOK`) comparable, and some merged via shared addresses — junk-block recall. Those renames have zero name overlap and are now honestly unreachable (identifier/acronym keys are the 2c fix). Boeing/Disney are now *compared* but score just below the 0.41 auto-merge threshold — a scoring/threshold concern for the address-handling track, not a blocking one. The ceiling's composition, not its number, was the real defect.

**The replace-verified gate earned its keep:** the plan predicted 93.1% assuming a pure 3-strategy set; the gate caught that this lost walmart's hyphen-split pairs (`WAL-MART` ↔ `WALMART`, covered only by `prefix`) plus the fake-reachable renames, and the 4-strategy set was chosen deliberately with the audit as evidence.

## Testing

- Canonicalizer: 31 rule-per-case tests (missed-pair collisions, ampersand collapse, `A O SMITH` guard, `SAB DE CV`/`BANCO DE CHILE`, mid-name suffix survival, punctuation-only placeholders).
- Fingerprint: key format, word-order, dedupe, negative path for unregistered semantic types.
- Phonetic: org-canonical-token contract, subset-name coverage (`APPLE COMPUTER INC` ↔ `APPLE INC`), person branches pinned unchanged.
- Audit-level: `Audit_NewStrategySet_ReachesBoeingAndSubsetPairs` proves the flip; the legacy instrument fixtures deliberately keep the old profile so the audit's miss-detection stays tested.
- Full solution suite: **556 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped** (Postgres integration ran).

## Out of scope (deferred by design)

Frequency-aware key suppression (spec 2b), rare-token/acronym/ngram keys and hyphen-variant fingerprints (spec 2c), scoring/threshold tuning and address handling (separate track), `samples/**` profiles (still on `token-name`; strategies remain registered).

items.title: fix(config): reject ambiguous Windows migration publications
items.body:
Fixes #221

## Root cause

The post-link migration checks compared default-number filesystem IDs. On Windows, those IDs can be lossy at JavaScript Number precision, allowing a concurrent replacement of the public candidate path to be mistaken for the private hard-linked candidate.

## Change

- Verify both backup and candidate hard-link publications with BigInt filesystem IDs.
- Fail closed when the exact inode identity is unavailable.
- Keep the existing held-source recovery and bounded CONFIG_MIGRATION_WRITE_FAILED behavior unchanged.

## TDD evidence

- Added a deterministic regression that aliases all default-number metadata after a concurrent target replacement while preserving the exact BigInt identity.
- The regression resolved before the exact-identity change and rejects afterward.
- Passed: config-migration focused suite, typecheck, lint.

Windows CI remains the authoritative validation for the original intermittent path.

items.title: feat(resources): audit / judge / eval — measure & prove knowledge-graph quality
items.body:
## Summary

Answers "how do we know the enrichment/links are any good?" with three measurement tiers (mapping to 2026 KG-eval practice: structural metrics + LLM-as-judge + retrieval eval).

- **T1 `resources audit [--json]`** — deterministic, no LLM: coverage %, connectivity (orphans, connected components, largest-component %, avg/max degree, density, hubs), integrity (dangling/self/duplicate links), distribution, and a **0–100 health score** + flags.
- **T2 `resources audit --judge [--sample N]`** — GraphJudge-style LLM-as-judge over sampled links → Zod-validated `{correct|weak|incorrect}` → **link precision**.
- **T3 `resources eval <set.json> [--json] | --generate`** — **precision@k / recall / nDCG** of ranked find vs an expected-set; planner can propose a candidate evalset. `EvalSetSchema` + extracted `rankFind`.

## Proven live (real 253-card graph, application-frontend)
```
healthScore 53/100 · 100% enriched/tagged · 36% linked · 144 orphans · 163 components · 0 dangling/self/dup
link precision (judged sample): weak, not wrong
```
i.e. the organization is measurably **sparse + loosely linked** — honest, quantified, and points at the next improvement (enrich's linking is too conservative).

## Test plan
- `tsc` clean; **256 vitest tests** (53 files).
- audit: fixture graph → exact orphans/components/density/dangling/self/dup + health-score monotonicity. judge: mocked verdicts → precision aggregation, malformed→unjudged, PlannerUnavailable→graceful. eval: hand-computed precision@k/recall/nDCG, malformed-set rejection. catalog anti-rot.

items.title: Blocking 2c: loose keys under suppression (token/acronym/ngram, 88.9% ceiling, prefix retired)
items.body:
## Summary

Final installment of the blocking-improvement track (spec 2c of 2a/2b/2c): **looser blocking keys, made safe by 2b's suppression**. Adds rare-token and acronym strategies, hyphen-variant fingerprinting, and per-token `ngram` for organizations; retires `prefix` from org profiles (replace-verified); ships the **first production use of `maxBlockSize`** (50) in the org and showcase profiles.

Showcase result: effective recall ceiling **87.5% → 88.9% (64/72)** with the missed set reduced to exactly the **8 pure corporate renames** (AT&T/SBC↔Southwestern Bell, Meta↔Facebook, Verizon↔Bell Atlantic — zero name overlap, closable in production via identifier-enabled CIK/LEI profiles, which the showcase deliberately forgoes). Achieved: **100% precision held, recall up 77.8% → 79.2% (F1 88.4)** — the SBC↔Southwestern Bell records now genuinely merge via a shared acronym key.

## What's included

- **Canonicalizer `Variants` seam** (`ITokenCanonicalizer.Variants`, default-implemented): primary tokens + hyphen-joined variant when different (`WAL-MART` ≡ `WALMART`), plus `CanonicalizeKeepingSuffixes` (the C in `SBC` comes from `CORP`, which normal canonicalization strips).
- **`token` strategy** (the Splink many-strict-keys model): one `token:{t}` key per canonical token of every variant, min length 2 — deliberately loose because 2b suppression caps common tokens. Closes the walmart hyphen-split class *without* `prefix`.
- **`acronym` strategy**: GENERATE initials from both suffix-keeping and suffix-stripped forms (2–6 tokens) + RECOGNIZE short alphabetic tokens as potential acronyms — the two rules meet at `acr:sbc`, flipping the one name-fixable missed pair.
- **Fingerprint hyphen-variants** via a shared `TokenCanonicalizers` map (single registration point for future taxonomies).
- **`ngram` for orgs — with a word-boundary fix** (see below).
- **Org profiles**: `["exact-value","fingerprint","phonetic","token","acronym","ngram"]` + `maxBlockSize: 50`; `prefix` retired from org profiles only (still registered; person profiles unchanged).
- Robustness fixtures pinning each class (hyphen, subset/reorder, typo, acronym) with **per-strategy contribution assertions** — reverting a strategy fails its class test even where older strategies also connect the pair.

## The gate catch (why measurement-first matters)

The first showcase re-run FAILED its hard gate: one incorrect merge — **Boeing + United Parcel Service**, precision 96.6%. Root cause, found via `match blocking explain`: `NGramBlockingStrategy` extracted trigrams from the space-stripped concatenation, so `UNITED PARCEL SERVICE INC` emitted the boundary-spanning junk gram `ngram:ein` (`SERVIC`**`E·IN`**`C`), colliding with BO**EIN**G's genuine trigram (block size 15 — under the suppression threshold, a *legit-sized junk block*). The pair then auto-merged on a shared Delaware registered-agent address.

Fix (user-approved scope amendment): **ngram keys are now generated per token and never span word boundaries** — the junk-gram class is eliminated at the source, within-word typo tolerance preserved, regression-pinned (`NGram_NeverSpansWordBoundaries`). The re-run passed every gate: 0 incorrect merges, 100% precision. The latent scoring fragility to shared registered-agent addresses is documented for the address/scoring track.

## Measured evidence (company-resolution showcase)

| Metric | Before (2b) | After (2c) |
|---|---|---|
| Effective recall ceiling | 87.5% (9 missed: 8 renames + SBC) | **88.9% (8 missed: all renames)** |
| Raw ceiling (no suppression) | 87.5% | 94.4% (suppression cost measured: 4 pairs via `ngram:inc`) |
| Achieved precision / recall / F1 | 100% / 77.8% / 87.5 | **100% / 79.2% / 88.4** |
| Incorrect merges | 0 | **0** |
| Candidate pairs | 71 | 2,563 (bounded; `ngram:inc` (61) suppressed by 2b) |
| CI gate | `--min-recall 0.87` | **`--min-recall 0.88`** (effective ceiling) |

## Testing

Canonicalizer variant/suffix-keeping tests; per-strategy unit tests (token emission/min-length, acronym generate+recognize+caps, fingerprint variants); the boundary-spanning regression test; four robustness-class fixtures with contribution attribution; full solution suite green (619+, Postgres ran); demo + `-AuditBlocking` exit 0.

## Out of scope (deferred by design)

Scoring/threshold changes (incl. the registered-agent address fragility → address track), identifier fields in the showcase, composite geo+token keys, person/product taxonomies, `samples/**` profiles.

items.title: Fix incorrect number_to_percentage default precision in docs [ci skip]
items.body:
### Motivation / Background

This Pull Request has been created because the RDoc for `number_to_percentage`
documents the wrong default for the `:precision` option. It states the option
"Defaults to 2", but percentage formatting actually defaults to a precision of 3.

The base number format default precision is 3
(`ActiveSupport::NumberHelper::NumberConverter::DEFAULTS[:format][:precision]`).
Only `:currency` overrides that to 2; the `:percentage` namespace overrides only
`:delimiter` and `:format`, so it inherits the base precision of 3. The method's
own doc examples already show three decimals
(`number_to_percentage(100) # => "100.000%"`), and the test suite asserts the same
(`number_to_percentage(100) == "100.000%"`), so the option description contradicted
both the examples directly above it and the actual behavior.

### Detail

This Pull Request changes a single line in the `number_to_percentage` documentation
in `activesupport/lib/active_support/number_helper.rb`: the `:precision` option
description now reads "Defaults to 3." instead of "Defaults to 2." The correct
"Defaults to 2." in the separate `number_to_currency` documentation is left
untouched.

```diff
     # [+:precision+]
     #   The level of precision, or +nil+ to preserve +number+'s precision.
-    #   Defaults to 2.
+    #   Defaults to 3.
     #
     #     number_to_percentage(12.3456789, precision: 4) # => "12.3457%"
```

### Additional information

Sources of truth confirming the default is 3 for percentage:

- `activesupport/lib/active_support/number_helper/number_converter.rb`:
  base `DEFAULTS[:format][:precision]` is 3; `currency` overrides it to 2; the
  `percentage` entry overrides only `:delimiter` and `:format` and therefore
  inherits 3.
- `activesupport/lib/active_support/locale/en.yml`: `number.format.precision` is 3;
  `number.currency.format.precision` is 2; `number.percentage.format` does not set
  `precision`, so it inherits 3.
- Existing tests corroborate the corrected default:
  `activesupport/test/number_helper_test.rb` and
  `activesupport/test/core_ext/numeric_ext_test.rb` both assert
  `number_to_percentage(100) == "100.000%"`.

The sibling helpers that also inherit the base default already document
"Defaults to 3." (`number_to_rounded`, `number_to_human_size`,
`number_to_human`); `number_to_percentage` was the only inconsistent one.

### Checklist

Before submitting the PR make sure the following are checked:

* [x] This Pull Request is related to one change. Unrelated changes should be opened in separate PRs.
* [x] Commit message has a detailed description of what changed and why.
* [ ] Tests are added or updated if you fix a bug or add a feature. (N/A: documentation-only change; existing tests already assert the corrected default.)
* [ ] CHANGELOG files are updated for the changed libraries if there is a behavior change or additional feature. (N/A: the template explicitly says documentation changes should not be included in the CHANGELOG.)

items.title: Raise on `quantization_config` + already-instantiated model in `DPOTrainer`/ `KTOTrainer`
items.body:
`DPOTrainer` accepts a `quantization_config` argument that is only meaningful when the model is loaded from a model identifier (`str`). That's the only point where `from_pretrained` runs and can apply it. When the policy is passed **already instantiated**, the config can't be applied to it, and the trainer only logged a warning saying it would be ignored.

But the warning didn't tell the whole story. The reference model is auto-created from `self.model.config` via `from_pretrained`, and that path *did* inject `quantization_config`. So in this scenario you silently ended up with:

- **policy** → full precision (config "ignored", as warned)
- **reference** → 4/8-bit (config quietly applied)

### Reproducer (previous behavior)

```python
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, BitsAndBytesConfig
from trl import DPOConfig, DPOTrainer
from datasets import load_dataset

# User builds the policy themselves (full precision) ...
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2-0.5B-Instruct")

dataset = load_dataset("trl-internal-testing/zen", "standard_preference", split="train")

# ... and also passes a quantization_config, expecting it to be ignored (as the warning says).
```

items.title: sdc-match: widen Wikitext↔SDC comparators to catch near-duplicate values
items.body:
## Summary

Widens the comparator paths that decide whether a community-contributed value (an inferred-from-Wikitext SDC claim, or a `{{DPLA metadata}}` template override) is really the same fact as DPLA's own value. Comparator-only changes — stored SDC values and rendered wikitext continue to match byte-for-byte.

## Motivating examples

- **[M174777532](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:1959-06_(June_1959)._The_John_Herron_Art_School_Chronicle_-_DPLA_-_89d2f0466a5b87a16332538b22acf4af_(page_1).jpg)** (indiana): P571 DPLA-side stored as `somevalue+P1932="June 1959"` alongside an inferred-from-Wikitext value-typed `+1959-06-01|P10`. Same fact, but `parse_dpla_date` rejected the month-name form → the somevalue side produced a `("p1932-string", …)` comparable while the value-typed side produced `("time", …)`. Shape mismatch, no dedup.
- **[M114630785](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Abbott,_A.D._-_DPLA_-_137b40c34543635bf3f145cd2f450227.jpg)** (bpl): P10358 description with a trailing `.` on the DPLA side vs. no trailing period on the community side. Byte comparison failed.
- **[M100761231](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:(Promissory_note_for_Thomas_Love)_-_DPLA_-_929a0beb5e9fe14c7f00b890dc05b966_(page_2).jpg)** (bpl): P1476 title bracketed `[…]` on the DPLA side (archival supplied-title convention) vs. unbracketed on the community side.
- **[M105419621](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:%22A_Barn_Yard%22_essay_for_English_IV_by_Sarah_(Sallie)_M._Field,_Abbot_Academy,_class_of_1904_-_DPLA_-_e4d34f37c00df7d514f7b320d537f94b_(page_1).jpg)** (bpl): No inferred SDC dupe. `{{DPLA metadata}}` carries `| date = 19 November 1902` next to canonical DPLA `1902-11-19`. `normalize_page` can't strip because `parse_dpla_date` rejects the natural-language form.

## Changes

- **`parse_dpla_date`** (`ingest_wikimedia/sdc.py`) accepts English month-name forms: `Month YYYY` (month precision), `Month D, YYYY` / `Month D YYYY` / `D Month YYYY` (day precision), plus `MM/DD/YYYY`. Every day-precision path runs `datetime.date(y, mo, d)` so phantom days (`February 30 1902`, `13/40/1900`) still fall back. Adjacent prose still forces fall-back — regexes anchored.
- **`casefold_for_compare(s)`** helper: strips leading/trailing whitespace + Unicode punctuation, collapses internal whitespace runs, casefolds. Applied ONLY as a comparator key.
- **`dates_semantically_equal(a, b)`** helper: True iff both parse to the same time+precision+circa-flag.
- **`_statement_comparable_value`** in `tools/sdc_sync.py`: text-shape branches (`string`, `monolingual`, `p1932-string`) fold their primary through `casefold_for_compare`. Reconciler still only removes inferred-from-Wikitext claims — never DPLA, never third-party.
- **`_value_matches`** in `ingest_wikimedia/wikitext_normalize.py`: two fallback paths after byte-equal + language-wrapper unwrap.
  - `param_name == "date"` → try `dates_semantically_equal`.
  - Display-string keys (`title` / `description` / `date` / `permission` / `creator`) → try folded equality.
  - Identifier keys (`hub` / `institution` / `url` / `dpla_id` / `local_id`) deliberately excluded — a case change in an opaque token is a distinct value.
- **`plan_migration`** in `ingest_wikimedia/legacy_artwork.py`: uses the same equivalence, so a community edit that only reformatted DPLA's own value (case, punctuation, or date format) is not imported as a spurious community contribution.

## Idempotency

No scrubber tool needed — the existing sdc-sync post-cleanup already re-runs `normalize_page` on every pass. Files carrying already-embedded near-duplicate overrides collapse automatically on their next sync.

## Test plan

- [x] Existing 495-test suite green (was passing before the fix).
- [x] Extended: 834 tests total, all passing on EC2 (Python 3.13, pywikibot).
- [x] `ruff check` + `ruff format` clean on all changed files.
- New tests cover every failure mode in the motivating examples plus:
  - Casefold `_for_compare_` folds case but preserves internal punctuation (`"A.D. Abbott"` ≠ `"A D Abbott"`).
  - `dates_semantically_equal` rejects precision mismatch (`1902` ≠ `1902-11-19`) and circa-flag mismatch.
  - `parse_dpla_date` still returns None for month-name forms adjacent to prose (`"January 1945 AD"`, `"Jan 1945 or 1946"`).
  - `_value_matches` preserves URL / identifier keys under case change.
  - Reconciler preserves language-mismatched monolingualtext claims (`en` vs `es` same text).

Round 3 fixes addressing: model download page cant scroll, status bar still showing (Tauri setFullscreen not implemented for Android), false model-already-downloaded error from wrong default precision, and missing first-launch user guide.

## Changes

### 1. Model download page scroll (cant scroll up/down)
- **Root cause**: `pad.css` sets `html, body { overflow: hidden }` globally which overrides `modelDownload.css` `body { overflow-y: auto }` (equal specificity, later in cascade wins)
- **Fix**: Add `overflow-y: auto !important` to modelDownload.css body

### 2. Status bar still showing (Android immersive mode didnt work)
- **Root cause**: Tauri 2 `setFullscreen(true)` is not implemented for the Android window plugin. The call succeeds but does nothing.
- **Fix**: JS-based safe-area detection in MainWindowApp onMounted: compare `window.screen.height` with `window.innerHeight` to calculate status bar height. Inject as `--safe-area-top` CSS variable on `:root` so toolbar `padding-top` uses the real value. Listens to resize/orientationchange.

### 3. False model-already-downloaded error
- **Root cause**: Default precision was `int8-npu` (DirectML NPU, desktop-only). On mobile, `model_download_check_version(int8-npu)` checks the wrong directory / returns incorrect results because the precision path doesnt exist on Android.
- **Fix**: Add `getDefaultPrecision()` returning `int8` on mobile, `int8-npu` on desktop. Fix `handlePrecision` fallback to use platform-aware default.

### 4. First-launch onboarding guide
- **New file**: `OnboardingOverlay.vue` - 3-step modal:
  1. Welcome / app intro

  3. Model download prompt (navigates to model download page)

Second fresh-eyes round — residual correctness gaps in the new poll/dedup logic:

Followup to #7245.
Turns out "but no cockpit actually needs micrometer or even nanometer precision" was an incorrect assumption, as this level of precision is needed to avoid shadow banding at very shallow light angles.

Fortunately, this is a very easy fix.
We just switch to linear handling in the closest accuracy band (thanks to Wookiee for the idea and find).
This will reduce the accuracy at 10m compared to Z-compressed, but not below what the accuracy was before Z-compression was introduced.
This will also not increase the accuracy of very close geometry to / beyond of what it was originally, but it will increase it beyond what it was with Z-compression.
In effect, this will just reshuffle some 10m accuracy to the sub-meter range in a linear fashion instead of in an equidistant fashion. This should remove any shadow banding in the cockpit range, while not reducing visual fidelity beyond what it was before Z-compression.

Any other parts of Z-compression, like long-distance view support or increased accuracy in the main battle lighting resolution are untouched and continue to work.

items.title: tolowerequalfold: avoid false positives on `ToLower(x) == x` / `!= x` case-detection idioms
items.body:
`tolowerequalfold` was flagging comparisons where one side is `strings.ToLower/ToUpper` and the other is the same operand, e.g. `strings.ToLower(x) != x`. Those are case-detection checks, not case-insensitive equality checks, and rewriting to `strings.EqualFold` can produce incorrect logic.

- **Analyzer precision: self-comparison guard**
  - Added a guard in `pkg/linters/tolowerequalfold/tolowerequalfold.go` to skip diagnostics when:
    - one side is `strings.ToLower/ToUpper(E)`, and
    - the other side is the same identifier `E` (matched via `types.Object` identity).
  - Refactored call detection with `caseConvArg(...)` and reused it from `isCaseConvCall(...)`.

- **Fixture coverage for the missed idiom**
  - Extended `pkg/linters/tolowerequalfold/testdata/src/tolowerequalfold/tolowerequalfold.go` `okExamples` with:
    - `strings.ToLower(name) == name`
    - `strings.ToLower(name) != name`
  - Existing flagged examples remain unchanged (e.g. comparisons against literals / different expressions).

```go
if arg, ok := caseConvArg(expr.X); ok && sameOperand(pass, arg, expr.Y) {
    return // case-detection idiom: do not suggest EqualFold
}
if arg, ok := caseConvArg(expr.Y); ok && sameOperand(pass, expr.X, arg) {
    return
}
if isCaseConvCall(expr.X) || isCaseConvCall(expr.Y) {
    pass.ReportRangef(expr, "use strings.EqualFold ...")
}
```

items.title: fix(billing): use persisted timezone and half-open ranges
items.body:
## Summary

Persist the Billing report timezone on the backend and standardize Billing queries on half-open time ranges.

## Why

Billing reports need one server-defined timezone for calendar-day boundaries and daily grouping. Relying on request defaults or inclusive end timestamps can:

- Split one local calendar day across multiple UTC dates.
- Make “Today” inconsistent between clients.
- Depend on `23:59:59.999999999` precision.
- Produce incorrect boundaries across 23-hour and 25-hour DST days.

## Changes

- Add `report_timezone` to the DB-backed Billing settings.
- Default the report timezone to `UTC`.
- Validate configured values as supported IANA timezone names.
- Apply timezone precedence in Management Billing:
  1. Request `timezone` override.
  2. Persisted `report_timezone`.
  3. `UTC`.
- Apply the resolved timezone to:
  - `/billing/overview`
  - `/billing/charges`
  - `/billing/balance-records`
- Standardize Billing ranges as `[from,to)`:
  - `from` is included.
  - `to` is excluded.
  - A date-only `to` becomes the next local midnight.
- Replace inclusive `created_at <= to` filters with `created_at < toExclusive`.
- Return exact UTC boundaries through:
  - `overview.range.from_at`
  - `overview.range.to_at_exclusive`
- Align authenticated User Billing routes with the same half-open range semantics.
- Update Management API and User API documentation in English and Chinese.

## API Contract

`GET /billing/settings` now includes:

```json
{
  "service_tier_source": "request",
  "report_timezone": "UTC"
}

PATCH /billing/settings accepts partial updates:

{
  "report_timezone": "Asia/Shanghai"
}

Billing overview ranges now expose both calendar labels and exact UTC boundaries:

{
  "range": {
    "from": "2026-07-19",
    "to": "2026-07-19",
    "from_at": "2026-07-18T16:00:00Z",
    "to_at_exclusive": "2026-07-19T16:00:00Z",
    "timezone": "Asia/Shanghai"
  }
}

## Compatibility Note

This intentionally changes explicit Billing to timestamps from inclusive to exclusive semantics.

Clients that previously sent the final nanosecond of a day should instead send the next calendar boundary. Date-only requests continue to include the complete selected day.

The reporting timezone only affects report boundaries and grouping. It does not reprice historical charges, rewrite price snapshots, or modify user balances.

## Validation

- go test -count=1 ./internal/cluster ./internal/cluster/management ./internal/userapi
- go build ./cmd/home

Added coverage for:

- Persisted timezone defaults and updates.
- Request timezone overrides.
- Invalid IANA timezone rejection.
- Exact exclusive-boundary exclusion.
- 23-hour and 25-hour DST calendar days.
- Management and User Billing range behavior.
```

items.title: fix(burn-train): correctly aggregate per-epoch metrics that require global statistics

### Checklist

- [ ] Confirmed that `cargo run-checks` command has been executed.
- [ ] Made sure the book is up to date with changes in this PR.

### Related Issues/PRs

Fixes #2758

Previously, metrics like Precision, Recall, and AUROC incorrectly assumed that global epoch-level scores could be computed by averaging individual batch-level metrics (weighted by sample count in `NumericMetricState`). This approach is biased for metrics requiring global statistics and sometimes entirely incorrect for metrics like AUROC and AUC-PR which cannot be meaningfully evaluated per-batch.

### Changes

- **Updated `Numeric` Trait:** Changed `value()` and `running_value()` to return `Option<NumericEntry>` (returning `None` for epoch-only metrics mid-epoch) and added `final_value()` to retrieve the computed metric at epoch completion.
- **Split `Metric` Execution:** Updated the `Metric` trait to decouple batch steps (`update`) from epoch-level finalization (`compute`). Updated `NumericMetricState` with `compute_update` and `compute_final` methods so that global aggregation is explicitly triggered at the end of each epoch (`end_epoch_train` in the event processor).
- **Added `ConfusionStatsState`:** Introduced a state structure that aggregates raw confusion matrix statistics (TP, FP, FN) across batches, enabling accurate global metric evaluation.
- **Updated `AurocMetric` & `AucPrMetric` via `PredictionAccumulatorState`:** Refactored `AurocMetric` to use `PredictionAccumulatorState` alongside `AucPrMetric`, accumulating raw prediction/target tensors during `update` and evaluating AUROC once over the full dataset during `compute`.

items.title: Preserve extended-precision temporal track IDs
items.body:
## What changed

- handle NumPy floating scalars before the generic `numbers.Real` path
- convert integral NumPy scalars directly with `int(value)` instead of first narrowing them to Python `float`
- preserve the string representation of fractional NumPy scalars whose mantissa exceeds Python `float` precision
- add a regression proving that adjacent `np.longdouble` track IDs above `2**53` remain distinct

`canonical_track_id()` converted every real-valued scalar through Python `float`. On platforms where `np.longdouble` has a wider mantissa, distinct tracker IDs such as `9007199254740992` and `9007199254740993` therefore collapsed to the same binary64 value before canonicalization.

Temporal continuation priors can now distinguish extended-precision tracker identifiers instead of incorrectly rewarding transitions between different tracks.

## Validation

- reproduced the identity collision with `np.longdouble` above `2**53`
- verified the corrected canonical IDs in an isolated Python check
- added a targeted pytest regression; it skips only on platforms where `longdouble` provides no precision beyond Python `float`

I hereby agree to the terms of the [GreptimeDB CLA](https://github.com/GreptimeTeam/.github/blob/main/CLA.md).

## Refer to a related PR or issue link (optional)

## What's changed and what's your intention?

This PR fixes two window sort issues around time-index sorting:

1. Window sort could fail to recognize aliased or wrapped time-index expressions, so some queries that should use the `WindowedSortExec` path would fall back to a normal sort plan.
2. Precision conversion between partition ranges and sort expressions could introduce an off-by-one boundary issue when timestamp precision changes, especially around exclusive range ends.

To address this, this PR:

- improves time-index expression tracking in `WindowedSortPhysicalRule`
- allows wrapped time-index expressions such as direct aliases, casts, and supported `to_timestamp_*` wrappers to be recognized as sortable time-index expressions
- fixes precision conversion for partition/time ranges used by window sort
- ensures exclusive end bounds are rounded correctly during timestamp unit conversion
- adds targeted unit tests for alias tracking and precision-boundary behavior
- adds sqlness regression coverage for the alias/wrapper cases in both standalone and distributed modes

A notable testing detail is that standalone and distributed produce slightly different `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` plans for wrapped expressions like `to_timestamp_millis(ts)`, so the sqlness cases are split per mode instead of sharing a common expected result.

## Why this matters

Queries such as the following should still benefit from window sort optimization:

- `SELECT ts AS ts ... ORDER BY ts`
- `SELECT to_timestamp_millis(ts) AS ts ... ORDER BY ts`

Without this fix, these queries may miss the optimized window sort path. Also, incorrect precision projection at range boundaries can cause rows near the end of a range to be sliced incorrectly.

## Testing

- added unit tests for:
  - alias tracking through projection
  - wrapped/casted time-index expression tracking
  - exclusive-end precision conversion
  - boundary preservation after precision conversion
- added sqlness regression tests for `windowed_sort_advance`

By default, Unity's `Vector3.ToString()` rounds coordinate values to a single decimal place (F1). When used to generate dictionary keys for spatial groupings (e.g., in a grid with a small cell size), distinct cells can map to the same string key, resulting in hash collisions and incorrectly grouped renderers. This commit explicitly sets the precision to "F5", resolving the grouping collision.

items.title: [libc_math] Fix libm special values and precision
items.body:
## Summary

Fixes incorrect special values and precision loss in the bundled math library
(`libm.a`, from the `libc_math` crate). Guests link this libm exclusively, so its
accuracy is the single source of truth for floating-point math. The affected
routines are replaced with faithful fdlibm/musl ports, and a POSIX C test suite
is added to guard against regressions.

closes #2810

## What changed

**Libraries (`libc_math`):** rewrite `fmod`, `exp`, `expm1`, `log`, `tanh`, `tan`,
`erf`, and `erfc` as fdlibm/musl ports.

- `fmod`: `fmod(x, ±inf) == x` and `fmod(±0, y)` preserves the sign of zero, via
  exact integer-significand division (previously returned NaN).
- `tanh`: preserves the sign of a zero argument (`tanh(-0.0) == -0.0`) and is
  evaluated through `expm1` to stay accurate near zero.
- `erfc`: evaluates the tail from a scaled exponential instead of `1 - erf(x)`,
  avoiding the catastrophic cancellation that destroyed precision for large `x`.
- `exp`, `expm1`, `log`, `tan`, `erf`: use the fdlibm minimax reductions,
  restoring ~1-ULP accuracy across their ranges.

**Tests:** add the `test-c-math` POSIX C suite validating IEEE-754 special values
and ~1-ULP accuracy for each function. Each call is laundered through a `volatile`
store so clang cannot constant-fold it at host precision under `-O3` and must emit
a real call into `libm.a`.

**Build and harness wiring:** register `test-c-math` in the guest POSIX test list
and add the suite (debug + release, terminal executor, exit code 0) to
`test/test-posix.toml` and `test/test-posix-windows.toml`.

## Validation

- `libc_math` host unit tests pass (356) and `cargo clippy` is clean.
- `test-c-math` boots under nanvixd in standalone mode and passes in both debug
  (`-O0`) and release (`-O3`).

## Why

Last week's PR #22 (live-taxonomy) worked mechanically — AI-only re-disposition suggestions dropped **95% → 5%** — but the flag rate barely moved (62% → ~56%). Live-data research showed descriptions aren't the lever (already populated; 1.2/1.3A/1.5 are described and still flag 67–83%); the remaining signal is the model disagreeing with the human's outcome label on real conversations.

**Product direction:** human agents do mis-disposition, and we want the AI to catch it using the transcript, call duration, and prior calls — including cases where a conversation happened but the outcome label is wrong. items.title: feat(scripts): backfill the risk-control calibration set from decision history
items.body:
Advances #8828.

The risk-control guarantee (#8835) needs adjudicated (confidence, correct?) pairs and the naive path is weeks of live label accrual. But `ai_review_cache` has retained per-finding confidence since 2026-06-28 and `review_audit` holds every acted gate decision — this backfill stages calibration candidates from that existing evidence, and adds the pre-registered α(n) tightening schedule so the published guarantee strengthens itself as labels accrue.

- **Pure core** (`scripts/backfill-decision-labels-core.ts`): acted closes stage as `close_arm` (a close whose realized outcome is `merged` = reopened-and-merged = the definitive incorrect class). Holds whose only blockers were AI-judgment findings stage as `holdout_close` for ANALYSIS only — adjudicating the backfill proved surviving holds are not valid close counterfactuals (a hold that survived means a non-confidence criterion blocked the close), so apply inserts close_arm rows only; the live ε-holdout (#8831) samples the would-close population and stays the valid source going forward.
- **Thin IO wrapper**: stdin candidates → `{records, labels, worklist}`. Records reuse `buildDecisionRecord`/`canonicalJson` (byte-identical digests); `configDigest: "backfill:unavailable"` is the honest provenance sentinel; no decision-ledger writes (the chain attests live finalizations only). Labels stage `status='pending'` — invisible to `loadCalibrationPairs` until adjudication flips them.
- **Pre-registered α(n) schedule** (`src/review/risk-control-wire.ts`): when no env α pins an arm, the close arm's budget follows a deterministic function of usable-label count — 0.05 under 350 pairs, 0.025 from 350, 0.015 from 700. Sample size is information, not the test statistic, so the walk is not outcome-snooping and each daily recalibration still runs exactly one level-δ test; the homepage claim self-tightens 95% → 97.5% → 98.5% with zero human steps. (The α-grid alternative needs a Bonferroni δ-split that raises every floor ~35% and certifies nothing at today's volume.)

Ran against production history: 653 candidates → 331 staged (232 close_arm, 99 analysis-only holdout_close), 280 mixed-blocker holds excluded, 42 duplicates deduped. Adjudicated close_arm set: 226 usable pairs, 9 incorrect (96.0% acted-close precision, coherent with the published 95.7% baseline); at today's volume the schedule's first tier certifies λ̂=0.62 at 57% coverage.

items.title: feat: measure reviewer precision/recall and feed policy tuning
items.body:
## Summary

Measures Athena's reviewer precision/recall against realized outcomes (postmortem decisionQualityLabels) and feeds the metrics back into the self-improvement policy tuning loop.

## Changes

### \src/core/athena_reviewer.ts\
- **\computeReviewerPrecisionRecall(postmortems)\** — pure function computing:
  - \precision\ = (correct + delayed_correct) / known_outcomes
  - \ecall\ = correct / (correct + delayed_correct)  
  - \ alsePositiveRate\ = incorrect / known_outcomes
  - \eworkRate\ = delayed_correct / (correct + delayed_correct)
  - \ 1\ = harmonic mean of precision and recall
  - \inconclusive\ entries excluded from all rate calculations

### \src/core/self_improvement.ts\
- **\REVIEWER_POLICY_THRESHOLDS\** — frozen enum of tuning thresholds (FP_RATE_HIGH=0.25, REWORK_RATE_HIGH=0.35, PRECISION_LOW=0.65)
- **\deriveReviewerPolicyAdjustment(metrics)\** — emits policySignal ('tighten'|'deepen'|'ok'), warning strings, lesson objects, and a suggested planQualityMinScore when thresholds are breached
- **\persistReviewerMetrics(config, metrics)\** — persists rolling history to \state/reviewer_metrics.json\ (capped at 100 entries, non-fatal)
- **\unSelfImprovementCycle\** — step 8 added: reads full postmortem history, computes precision/recall, persists metrics, derives policy adjustments and injects lessons into knowledge memory

### \src/core/carry_forward_ledger.ts\
- **\createReviewerDebtIfNeeded(ledger, metrics, cycle, opts)\** — creates a \critical\ carry-forward debt entry when FP rate exceeds threshold (default 30%) and sample >= 5 known outcomes; guards against duplicate open entries

### \	ests/core/athena_reviewer_precision_recall.test.ts\ (new)
22 tests covering all acceptance criteria:
- All-correct → precision=1, recall=1, fpr=0
- All-incorrect → precision=0, fpr=1, recall=null
- Mixed labels → deterministic computation verified
- Inconclusive exclusion from rates
- Empty/null input → null rates, no crash
- Policy signal: tighten on high FP, deepen on high rework, critical lesson on low precision
- Debt creation, deduplication, sample size guard
- I/O persistence and 100-entry cap

## Test Evidence
- 3888 tests pass (22 new)
- Zero new lint errors introduced
- Latency benchmark (test 282) is pre-existing flaky test, unrelated to this change

items.title: fix: extreme-exponent handling in strtof import
items.body: Prevent incorrect clamping and loss of precision when parsing extreme exponents in po32_import_strtof. Keep zero mantissas (e.g. "0e39") as zero instead of saturating to FLT_MAX, and split large negative exponent scaling into two LUT calls to avoid po32_lut_pow10f saturation so values for exponents in the 39..45 range decrease monotonically. Added tests to cover zero-with-overflow cases and verify monotonic behavior for 1e-39, 1e-42, 1e-45 as well as existing underflow checks.
